sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Eógan Mór was a king of Munster, a southwestern province. Mór means great, and Mug Nuadat is another name for him. He was a husband of Beare, a legendary Spanish princess. Her name survives in the Beare peninsula. Eógan Mór long fought the king Conn of the Hundred Battles. The two kings clashed repeatedly near the frontier. Conn drove Eógan abroad, and Eógan fled to Spain. He came back to fight once more, but Conn slew him.
